Former FTX COO First Reveals: Justin Sun Offered $4B Rescue, Arriving ~10 Minutes After Bankruptcy Appointment Former FTX COO Constance Wang recalled in a post that after CZ announced he would sell FTT on November 6, 2022, roughly $6 billion left the platform within 72 hours. On November 8, she saw a massive negative figure at the bottom of the balance sheet; Binance then quickly walked away on Wednesday after receiving due diligence documents, and Bahamian regulators froze local entity assets the next day. Constance revealed that at around 4:40 a.m. on November 11, the team received a message from Justin Sun offering $4 billion in liquidity backed by the FTX Ventures portfolio—arriving roughly 10 minutes after SBF had signed the letter appointing John Ray as the new CEO. Although SBF tried to revoke the appointment, it was too late, and Ray took FTX and its affiliates into Chapter 11 bankruptcy hours later. — link

Highlight Clip: CZ: Negative Comments Could Discourage Vitalik CZ: Negative Comments Could Discourage Vitalik Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) said at BNB Bangkok Demo Night on November 27 that he has known Vitalik Buterin since 2013 and initially doubted he could build Ethereum. CZ believes crypto would be much smaller without Ethereum, possibly lacking ICOs and ERC-20 tokens. Binance launched in 2017, with BNB initially an Ethereum-based ERC-20 token before becoming native a few years later. CZ said negative comments about ETH's price might demotivate Vitalik, while more community encouragement could help him spend more time on Ethereum. He believes Vitalik remains committed to building it. — link
